classification.difficultyReason: Follow an explicit sequence linking factorisation, intercepts, root midpoint and substitution to sketch each parabola and classify its extremum; negative leading coefficients require sign control, but the decisions are scaffolded.

inlines.text: For each of the following quadratics
find the coordinates of the vertex.
state whether the vertex is a maximum or a minimum.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(x+4)(x-4)\\0&=(x+4)(x-4)\\x&=-4\text{ or }4\\y(0)&=0^2-16\\y(0)&=-16\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-4+4}{2}=0\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(0,-16)$, which is also the $y$-intercept. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-16$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with roots -4 and 4, and vertex/y-intercept -16 on the y-axis.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x(x+5)\\0&=x(x+5)\\x&=0\text{ or }-5\\y(0)&=0\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{0-5}{2}=-\frac52\\y\left(-\frac52\right)&=\left(-\frac52\right)\left(-\frac52+5\right)\\y\left(-\frac52\right)&=-\frac{25}4\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac52,-\frac{25}4)$. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-\frac{25}4$.

spec.description: Upward parabola through the origin with other root -5 and dashed vertex guides -5/2 and -25/4.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x(2x-5)\\0&=x(2x-5)\\x&=0\text{ or }\frac52\\y(0)&=0\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{0+\frac52}{2}=\frac54\\y\left(\frac54\right)&=\frac54\left(2\times\frac54-5\right)\\y\left(\frac54\right)&=-\frac{25}8\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(\frac54,-\frac{25}8)$. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-\frac{25}8$.

spec.description: Upward parabola through the origin and root 5/2, with dashed vertex guides 5/4 and -25/8.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(x+6)(x-2)\\0&=(x+6)(x-2)\\x&=-6\text{ or }2\\y(0)&=0^2+4(0)-12\\y(0)&=-12\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-6+2}{2}=-2\\y(-2)&=(-2+6)(-2-2)\\y(-2)&=-16\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-2,-16)$. The parabola opens upwards, so its minimum $y$-value is $-16$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with roots -6 and 2, axis guide -2, y-intercept -12 and minimum -16.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x^2+4x-12)\\y&=-(x+6)(x-2)\\0&=-(x+6)(x-2)\\x&=-6\text{ or }2\\y(0)&=12-4(0)-0^2\\y(0)&=12\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-6+2}{2}=-2\\y(-2)&=-(-2+6)(-2-2)\\y(-2)&=16\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-2,16)$. The parabola opens downwards, so its maximum $y$-value is $16$.

spec.description: Downward parabola with roots -6 and 2, axis guide -2, y-intercept 12 and maximum 16.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-x(x-8)\\0&=-x(x-8)\\x&=0\text{ or }8\\y(0)&=0\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{0+8}{2}=4\\y(4)&=-4(4-8)\\y(4)&=16\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(4,16)$. The parabola opens downwards, so its maximum $y$-value is $16$.

spec.description: Downward parabola through the origin and root 8, with dashed vertex guides at 4 and 16.
